title: Matn 1: Praise, Salah on the Prophet and Why We Learn Creed Young
interactive_html:
Your Goal: Know how the manẓūmah begins and why a child should learn correct belief early.

الْكَلِمَاتُ Words · tap to see the meaning

الْحَمْدُ
praising Allah with love and honour
الشُّكْرُ
thanking Allah with the heart, tongue and body
الصَّلَاةُ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ
asking Allah to honour and praise the Prophet ﷺ
الْعَقِيدَةُ
what the heart firmly believes
الْمَنْظُومَةُ
a text in verse, easy to memorise
الطِّفْلُ
child
الْحِفْظُ
memorising
النَّقْشُ
carving

الْفِكْرَةُ The idea in simple words

The manẓūmah begins the way scholars begin their books: with praise of Allah, then peace and blessings on the Prophet ﷺ. Then the author tells us why it was written: so that children grow up on correct belief. What we learn when we are young stays firm, like a carving in stone, so we start now.

الْحِفْظُ Memorise this part

Learn this part of the manẓūmah Talqīn al-ʿAqīdah lil-Aṭfāl (by Shaykh Yāsir Duḥaym) with your teacher. Recite it five times from the book, then try without looking.

جُمَلٌ نَقُولُهَا Sentences to learn · tap to see the meaning

الْحَمْدُ لِلهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ.
All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds. (Qur’an 1:2)
اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ.
O Allah, send blessings and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad.
الْعِلْمُ فِي الصِّغَرِ كَالنَّقْشِ فِي الْحَجَرِ.
Knowledge learned when young is like carving in stone.
أَحْفَظُ الْعَقِيدَةَ وَأَنَا صَغِيرٌ.
I memorise the creed while I am young.

تَدْرِيبٌ Practice

بِمَاذَا نَبْدَأُ كَلَامَنَا الْمُهِمَّ؟
Answer in Arabic: What do we begin important speech with?
الْجَوَابُ
بِالْحَمْدِ لِلهِ وَالصَّلَاةِ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ.
كَيْفَ نَشْكُرُ اللهَ؟
Answer in Arabic: How do we thank Allah?
الْجَوَابُ
بِقُلُوبِنَا وَأَلْسِنَتِنَا وَأَعْمَالِنَا.
لِمَاذَا نَحْفَظُ الْعَقِيدَةَ صِغَارًا؟
Answer in Arabic: Why do we memorise creed when young?
الْجَوَابُ
لِأَنَّ الْعِلْمَ فِي الصِّغَرِ كَالنَّقْشِ فِي الْحَجَرِ.

title: Matn 2: Where Our Belief Comes From
interactive_html:
Your Goal: Name the sources of belief and say why we follow the understanding of the first generations.

الْكَلِمَاتُ Words · tap to see the meaning

الْقُرْآنُ
the Book of Allah
السُّنَّةُ
the Prophet’s ﷺ sayings, actions and approvals
الصَّحَابَةُ
the Companions
الدَّلِيلُ
proof / evidence
الْفَهْمُ
understanding
الْقُرُونُ الْأُولَى
the first generations of Muslims

الْفِكْرَةُ The idea in simple words

What we believe about Allah, the angels, the books, the messengers and the Last Day does not come from opinions or imagination. It comes from the Qur’an and the authentic Sunnah, understood the way the Companions and the first generations understood them. They saw revelation come down and learned straight from the Prophet ﷺ, so their understanding is the safest road.

الْحِفْظُ Memorise this part

Learn this part of the manẓūmah Talqīn al-ʿAqīdah lil-Aṭfāl (by Shaykh Yāsir Duḥaym) with your teacher. Recite it five times from the book, then try without looking.

جُمَلٌ نَقُولُهَا Sentences to learn · tap to see the meaning

عَقِيدَتِي مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ وَالسُّنَّةِ.
My belief comes from the Qur’an and the Sunnah.
تَعَلَّمَ الصَّحَابَةُ الدِّينَ مِنَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ.
The Companions learned the religion from the Prophet ﷺ.
لَا أَتَكَلَّمُ فِي الدِّينِ بِلَا دَلِيلٍ.
I do not speak about the religion without proof.

تَدْرِيبٌ Practice

مَا مَصْدَرُ الْعَقِيدَةِ؟
Answer in Arabic: What is the source of belief?
الْجَوَابُ
الْقُرْآنُ وَالسُّنَّةُ بِفَهْمِ الصَّحَابَةِ.
مَنْ عَلَّمَ الصَّحَابَةَ؟
Answer in Arabic: Who taught the Companions?
الْجَوَابُ
عَلَّمَهُمُ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ.
هَلْ أَقُولُ فِي الدِّينِ بِرَأْيِي؟
Answer in Arabic: May I speak about religion by my own opinion?
الْجَوَابُ
لَا، أَطْلُبُ الدَّلِيلَ.

title: Matn 3: Who Is Your Lord?
interactive_html:
Your Goal: Say who your Lord is and give three proofs from daily life: He created, He provides, He controls.

الْكَلِمَاتُ Words · tap to see the meaning

الرَّبُّ
the Lord: Creator, Owner and Sustainer
الْخَالِقُ
the Creator
الرَّازِقُ
the Provider
الْمُدَبِّرُ
the One who arranges all affairs
الْمَخْلُوقَاتُ
creations
الْإِنْسَانُ
human being

الْفِكْرَةُ The idea in simple words

The first question every person is asked is: who is your Lord? Our Lord is Allah. He created us and everything around us, He gives us food, air and water, and He arranges every matter. Nobody else created even a fly. Allah says: “Allah is the Creator of all things.” (Qur’an 39:62)

الْحِفْظُ Memorise this part

Learn this part of the manẓūmah Talqīn al-ʿAqīdah lil-Aṭfāl (by Shaykh Yāsir Duḥaym) with your teacher. Recite it five times from the book, then try without looking.

جُمَلٌ نَقُولُهَا Sentences to learn · tap to see the meaning

رَبِّيَ اللهُ.
My Lord is Allah.
اللهُ خَلَقَنِي وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ.
Allah created me and created everything.
اللهُ يَرْزُقُنِي وَيَرْزُقُ الْجَمِيعَ.
Allah provides for me and for everyone.
اللهُ يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ.
Allah arranges every affair.

تَدْرِيبٌ Practice

مَنْ رَبُّكَ؟
Answer in Arabic: Who is your Lord?
الْجَوَابُ
رَبِّيَ اللهُ.
مَنْ خَلَقَكَ؟
Answer in Arabic: Who created you?
الْجَوَابُ
خَلَقَنِي اللهُ.
مَنْ يَرْزُقُكَ؟
Answer in Arabic: Who provides for you?
الْجَوَابُ
يَرْزُقُنِي اللهُ.

title: Matn 4: The Three Kinds of Tawhid
interactive_html:
Your Goal: Name the three kinds of Tawhid and say in one sentence what each one means.

الْكَلِمَاتُ Words · tap to see the meaning

التَّوْحِيدُ
making Allah One in everything that is His right
تَوْحِيدُ الرُّبُوبِيَّةِ
Allah alone is Lord: Creator, Provider, Controller
تَوْحِيدُ الْأُلُوهِيَّةِ
Allah alone is worshipped
تَوْحِيدُ الْأَسْمَاءِ وَالصِّفَاتِ
believing in Allah’s names and attributes as He described Himself
الشِّرْكُ
giving someone a share in what belongs only to Allah
الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَى
the most beautiful names of Allah

الْفِكْرَةُ The idea in simple words

Tawhid has three parts. One: Allah alone is the Lord who creates, provides and controls. Two: Allah alone deserves worship, so prayer, du‘ā’ and every act of worship are for Him only. Three: we believe in Allah’s names and attributes exactly as He and His Messenger ﷺ described Him, without comparing Him to creation and without denying what He affirmed. Allah says: “There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.” (Qur’an 42:11)

الْحِفْظُ Memorise this part

Learn this part of the manẓūmah Talqīn al-ʿAqīdah lil-Aṭfāl (by Shaykh Yāsir Duḥaym) with your teacher. Recite it five times from the book, then try without looking.

جُمَلٌ نَقُولُهَا Sentences to learn · tap to see the meaning

اللهُ وَاحِدٌ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ.
Allah is One; He has no partner.
أَعْبُدُ اللهَ وَحْدَهُ.
I worship Allah alone.
لِلهِ الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَى.
To Allah belong the most beautiful names.
لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ.
There is nothing like Him.

تَدْرِيبٌ Practice

كَمْ قِسْمًا لِلتَّوْحِيدِ؟
Answer in Arabic: How many kinds of Tawhid are there?
الْجَوَابُ
ثَلَاثَةُ أَقْسَامٍ: الرُّبُوبِيَّةُ وَالْأُلُوهِيَّةُ وَالْأَسْمَاءُ وَالصِّفَاتُ.
مَا تَوْحِيدُ الْأُلُوهِيَّةِ؟
Answer in Arabic: What is Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah?
الْجَوَابُ
أَنْ نَعْبُدَ اللهَ وَحْدَهُ.
هَلْ يُشْبِهُ اللهُ خَلْقَهُ؟
Answer in Arabic: Is Allah like His creation?
الْجَوَابُ
لَا، لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ.

title: Matn 5: Worship and Its Two Conditions
interactive_html:
Your Goal: Know that all worship is for Allah alone and say the two conditions for it to be accepted.

الْكَلِمَاتُ Words · tap to see the meaning

الْعِبَادَةُ
everything Allah loves of words and deeds, outward and inward
الصَّلَاةُ
prayer
الصِّيَامُ
fasting
الدُّعَاءُ
calling upon Allah
الْإِخْلَاصُ
sincerity: doing it for Allah alone
الْمُتَابَعَةُ
following the Prophet ﷺ

الْفِكْرَةُ The idea in simple words

Worship includes prayer, fasting, du‘ā’ and many more acts. It belongs to Allah alone: “You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.” (Qur’an 1:5) For worship to be accepted it needs two conditions. Sincerity: we do it only for Allah, not to show off. Following: we do it the way the Prophet ﷺ taught us, with no additions or cuts. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Actions are only by intentions.” (al-Bukhārī and Muslim)

الْحِفْظُ Memorise this part

Learn this part of the manẓūmah Talqīn al-ʿAqīdah lil-Aṭfāl (by Shaykh Yāsir Duḥaym) with your teacher. Recite it five times from the book, then try without looking.

جُمَلٌ نَقُولُهَا Sentences to learn · tap to see the meaning

إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ.
You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.
أُصَلِّي لِلهِ وَحْدَهُ.
I pray for Allah alone.
أَعْمَلُ بِإِخْلَاصٍ وَأَتَّبِعُ سُنَّةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ.
I act with sincerity and follow the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ.

تَدْرِيبٌ Practice

لِمَنْ نَصْرِفُ الْعِبَادَةَ؟
Answer in Arabic: To whom do we direct worship?
الْجَوَابُ
لِلهِ وَحْدَهُ.
مَا شَرْطَا قَبُولِ الْعِبَادَةِ؟
Answer in Arabic: What are the two conditions for worship to be accepted?
الْجَوَابُ
الْإِخْلَاصُ وَالْمُتَابَعَةُ.
اذْكُرْ ثَلَاثَ عِبَادَاتٍ.
Answer in Arabic: Name three acts of worship.
الْجَوَابُ
الصَّلَاةُ وَالصِّيَامُ وَالدُّعَاءُ.

title: Matn 6: Our Duties to the Prophet ﷺ, His Family and the Companions
title_ar: حُقُوقُ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ وَآلِ الْبَيْتِ وَالصَّحَابَةِ
interactive_html:
Your Goal: Name our four duties to the Prophet ﷺ, say who we love after him, and learn the closing du‘ā’ of the manẓūmah.

الْكَلِمَاتُ Words · tap to see the meaning

الْمَحَبَّةُ
love
الطَّاعَةُ
obedience
التَّعْظِيمُ
honouring and respect
النُّصْرَةُ
support and defence
آلُ الْبَيْتِ
the family of the Prophet ﷺ
الْفَوْزُ
success

الْفِكْرَةُ The idea in simple words

Our duties to the Prophet ﷺ are love, obedience, honour and support, by following his Sunnah and defending his good name. The Prophet ﷺ said: “None of you truly believes until I am dearer to him than his father, his child and all people.” (al-Bukhārī) We also love his family and his Companions, who saw the revelation with their own eyes and carried the religion to us. The manẓūmah ends by asking Allah for sincerity and for Paradise.

الْحِفْظُ Memorise this part

Learn this part of the manẓūmah Talqīn al-ʿAqīdah lil-Aṭfāl (by Shaykh Yāsir Duḥaym) with your teacher. Recite it five times from the book, then try without looking.

جُمَلٌ نَقُولُهَا Sentences to learn · tap to see the meaning

أُحِبُّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ وَأُطِيعُهُ.
I love the Prophet ﷺ and obey him.
أُحِبُّ آلَ الْبَيْتِ وَالصَّحَابَةَ.
I love the family of the Prophet and the Companions.
اللَّهُمَّ ارْزُقْنَا الْإِخْلَاصَ وَالْجَنَّةَ.
O Allah, grant us sincerity and Paradise.

تَدْرِيبٌ Practice

مَا حُقُوقُ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ عَلَيْنَا؟
Answer in Arabic: What are the Prophet’s ﷺ rights over us?
الْجَوَابُ
الْمَحَبَّةُ وَالطَّاعَةُ وَالتَّعْظِيمُ وَالنُّصْرَةُ.
مَنْ نُحِبُّ بَعْدَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ؟
Answer in Arabic: Who do we love after the Prophet ﷺ?
الْجَوَابُ
آلَ الْبَيْتِ وَالصَّحَابَةَ.
مَاذَا نَسْأَلُ اللهَ فِي الْخِتَامِ؟
Answer in Arabic: What do we ask Allah at the end?
الْجَوَابُ
الْإِخْلَاصَ وَالْجَنَّةَ.

title: Mahfūdhāt 1: Imam ash-Shāfiʿī — Patience When Days Turn
interactive_html:
Your Goal: Recite three verses attributed to Imam ash-Shāfiʿī and learn to stay calm and generous when life is hard.

نَبْذَةٌ About the poet

Imam Muḥammad ibn Idrīs ash-Shāfiʿī (150–204 AH) was the founder of the Shāfiʿī school of fiqh and one of the most eloquent speakers of Arabic among the scholars. These verses are widely attributed to him.

الْأَبْيَاتُ Verses · tap to see the meaning

دَعِ الْأَيَّامَ تَفْعَلُ مَا تَشَاءُ … وَطِبْ نَفْسًا إِذَا حَكَمَ الْقَضَاءُ
Let the days do what they will, and be at ease when the decree comes.
وَلَا تَجْزَعْ لِحَادِثَةِ اللَّيَالِي … فَمَا لِحَوَادِثِ الدُّنْيَا بَقَاءُ
Do not grieve at what the nights bring, for the events of this world do not last.
وَكُنْ رَجُلًا عَلَى الْأَهْوَالِ جَلْدًا … وَشِيمَتُكَ السَّمَاحَةُ وَالْوَفَاءُ
Be steady in times of fear, and let generosity and loyalty be your character.

الْكَلِمَاتُ Words · tap to see the meaning

دَعِ
leave / let
الْقَضَاءُ
the decree of Allah
تَجْزَعْ
you grieve / panic
الْحَوَادِثُ
events
جَلْدٌ
steady, strong
شِيمَةٌ
character
السَّمَاحَةُ
generosity
الْوَفَاءُ
loyalty

الْحِكْمَةُ The hikmah

Hard days come and go. A believer stays calm because he trusts Allah’s decree, and keeps his good character: generous with people and loyal to his word. Being calm does not mean doing nothing; it means we work, then we accept what Allah decides.

قَاعِدَةٌ Grammar spotlight

Commands: دَعِ (leave), طِبْ (be at ease) and كُنْ (be) are all command verbs. Don’t: لَا + verb means “do not”, and the verb ends with a sukūn: لَا تَجْزَعْ.

تَدْرِيبٌ Practice

كَيْفَ نَقُولُ: Do not grieve?
Say in Arabic: Do not grieve.
الْجَوَابُ
لَا تَجْزَعْ.
مَا صِفَتَانِ يُحِبُّهُمَا الشَّاعِرُ فِي الرَّجُلِ؟
Answer in Arabic: Which two qualities does the poet love in a man?
الْجَوَابُ
السَّمَاحَةُ وَالْوَفَاءُ.
هَلْ تَبْقَى حَوَادِثُ الدُّنْيَا؟
Answer in Arabic: Do the events of this world stay forever?
الْجَوَابُ
لَا، مَا لَهَا بَقَاءٌ.

title: Mahfūdhāt 2: Imam ash-Shāfiʿī — The Fault Is in Us
interactive_html:
Your Goal: Recite two verses attributed to Imam ash-Shāfiʿī and learn to look at our own faults before blaming others.

نَبْذَةٌ About the poet

Imam ash-Shāfiʿī (150–204 AH) is known for wise short poems about character and knowledge. These verses are widely attributed to him.

الْأَبْيَاتُ Verses · tap to see the meaning

نَعِيبُ زَمَانَنَا وَالْعَيْبُ فِينَا … وَمَا لِزَمَانِنَا عَيْبٌ سِوَانَا
We blame our time while the fault is in us; our time has no fault but us.
وَنَهْجُو ذَا الزَّمَانِ بِغَيْرِ ذَنْبٍ … وَلَوْ نَطَقَ الزَّمَانُ لَنَا هَجَانَا
We scold this time though it did nothing wrong; if time could speak, it would scold us.

الْكَلِمَاتُ Words · tap to see the meaning

نَعِيبُ
we blame
الزَّمَانُ
time / the age
الْعَيْبُ
fault / flaw
سِوَى
other than
نَهْجُو
we scold / mock
ذَنْبٌ
sin / wrongdoing
نَطَقَ
spoke

الْحِكْمَةُ The hikmah

When things go wrong it is easy to blame “the times”, other people or bad luck. The poet teaches us to look inside first: What did I do? What can I fix in myself? A person who checks himself grows; a person who only blames others stays stuck.

قَاعِدَةٌ Grammar spotlight

The ending ـنَا means “our / us”, just like the attached pronouns you learned in Arabiyyah: زَمَانَنَا (our time), فِينَا (in us), سِوَانَا (other than us), هَجَانَا (it would scold us).

تَدْرِيبٌ Practice

مَاذَا تَعْنِي كَلِمَةُ «زَمَانَنَا»؟
Answer: What does زَمَانَنَا mean?
الْجَوَابُ
وَقْتَنَا — our time.
أَيْنَ الْعَيْبُ كَمَا يَقُولُ الشَّاعِرُ؟
Answer in Arabic: Where is the fault, according to the poet?
الْجَوَابُ
الْعَيْبُ فِينَا.
كَيْفَ نَقُولُ: in us؟
Say in Arabic: in us
الْجَوَابُ
فِينَا.

title: Mahfūdhāt 3: The Six Keys to Knowledge
interactive_html:
Your Goal: Recite two verses on the six things a student needs to gain knowledge, and name all six.

نَبْذَةٌ About the verses

These famous verses are attributed to Imam ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may Allah be pleased with him) and are also reported from Imam ash-Shāfiʿī; scholars mention both. They are among the most memorised verses for students of knowledge.

الْأَبْيَاتُ Verses · tap to see the meaning

أَخِي لَنْ تَنَالَ الْعِلْمَ إِلَّا بِسِتَّةٍ … سَأُنْبِيكَ عَنْ تَفْصِيلِهَا بِبَيَانِ
My brother, you will never gain knowledge except through six things; I will tell you about them clearly.
ذَكَاءٍ وَحِرْصٍ وَاجْتِهَادٍ وَبُلْغَةٍ … وَصُحْبَةِ أُسْتَاذٍ وَطُولِ زَمَانِ
Intelligence, eagerness, effort, means to live on, the company of a teacher, and a long time.

الْكَلِمَاتُ Words · tap to see the meaning

ذَكَاءٌ
intelligence
حِرْصٌ
eagerness
اجْتِهَادٌ
hard work
بُلْغَةٌ
enough provision to live on
صُحْبَةُ أُسْتَاذٍ
staying with a teacher
طُولُ زَمَانٍ
a long time, patience

الْحِكْمَةُ The hikmah

Knowledge is not gained in a day. You need a clear mind, a real wish to learn, steady effort, enough to live on, a good teacher and patience over years. If you are missing one, work on it. Compare this with the Five Keys in your Arabiyyah course.

قَاعِدَةٌ Grammar spotlight

لَنْ + present verb means “will never”, and the verb ends with a fatḥa: لَنْ تَنَالَ. إِلَّا means “except”: لَنْ تَنَالَ الْعِلْمَ إِلَّا بِسِتَّةٍ.

تَدْرِيبٌ Practice

اذْكُرِ الْأَسْبَابَ السِّتَّةَ.
Answer in Arabic: Name the six things.
الْجَوَابُ
ذَكَاءٌ وَحِرْصٌ وَاجْتِهَادٌ وَبُلْغَةٌ وَصُحْبَةُ أُسْتَاذٍ وَطُولُ زَمَانٍ.
مَاذَا تَعْنِي «لَنْ تَنَالَ»؟
Answer: What does لَنْ تَنَالَ mean?
الْجَوَابُ
You will never gain.
مَا الْأَسْبَابُ الَّتِي أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى تَقْوِيَتِهَا؟
Think: Which of the six do I need to strengthen?
الْجَوَابُ
Your own answer, then tell your teacher.

title: Mahfūdhāt 4: Abū al-ʿAtāhiyah — This World Is Temporary
interactive_html:
Your Goal: Recite a verse commonly attributed to Abū al-ʿAtāhiyah and learn to prepare for the Hereafter.

نَبْذَةٌ About the poet

Abū al-ʿAtāhiyah (about 130–211 AH) was an Abbasid-era poet, famous for poems of zuhd, reminding people that this world is short. This verse is commonly attributed to him.

الْأَبْيَاتُ Verse · tap to see the meaning

لِدُوا لِلْمَوْتِ وَابْنُوا لِلْخَرَابِ … فَكُلُّكُمُ يَصِيرُ إِلَى تَبَابِ
Bear children for death and build for ruin; every one of you is heading to destruction.

الْكَلِمَاتُ Words · tap to see the meaning

لِدُوا
give birth (you all)
الْمَوْتُ
death
ابْنُوا
build (you all)
الْخَرَابُ
ruin
يَصِيرُ
goes to / ends up
تَبَابٌ
destruction, loss

الْحِكْمَةُ The hikmah

Whatever we build or collect in this world will end. The wise person uses the short time he has to do good deeds that stay with him in the Hereafter. This verse is a reminder, not a reason to give up on life: we still work, learn and build, but with the Hereafter in mind.

قَاعِدَةٌ Grammar spotlight

Commands to a group: لِدُوا and ابْنُوا end with ـوا, which means “you all”. Compare with the single command دَعِ in the first lesson. Also notice كُلُّكُمْ: كُلّ + كُمْ (all of you).

تَدْرِيبٌ Practice

كَيْفَ نَقُولُ: Build (you all)؟
Say in Arabic: Build! (to a group)
الْجَوَابُ
ابْنُوا.
إِلَى أَيْنَ يَصِيرُ كُلُّ إِنْسَانٍ فِي الدُّنْيَا؟
Answer: What does the poet say every person is heading to?
الْجَوَابُ
إِلَى الْمَوْتِ وَالْخَرَابِ.
مَاذَا نَعْمَلُ لِلْآخِرَةِ؟
Answer in Arabic: What do we do for the Hereafter?
الْجَوَابُ
نَعْمَلُ الْأَعْمَالَ الصَّالِحَةَ.

title: Mahfūdhāt 5: Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā — Character Always Shows
title_ar: زُهَيْرُ بْنُ أَبِي سُلْمَى: وَمَهْمَا تَكُنْ
interactive_html:
Your Goal: Recite two wise verses by Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā and learn how the word مَهْمَا works.

نَبْذَةٌ About the poet

Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā (died around 609 CE) lived before Islam and is one of the poets of the Muʿallaqāt. He is famous for wisdom. His son Kaʿb later became Muslim (see Lesson 8). We take his wise sayings and leave pre-Islamic customs.

الْأَبْيَاتُ Verses · tap to see the meaning

وَمَهْمَا تَكُنْ عِنْدَ امْرِئٍ مِنْ خَلِيقَةٍ … وَإِنْ خَالَهَا تَخْفَى عَلَى النَّاسِ تُعْلَمِ
Whatever trait a person has, even if he thinks it is hidden from people, it will become known.
سَئِمْتُ تَكَالِيفَ الْحَيَاةِ وَمَنْ يَعِشْ … ثَمَانِينَ حَوْلًا لَا أَبَا لَكَ يَسْأَمِ
I am tired of life’s burdens; whoever lives eighty years grows tired. (“لَا أَبَا لَكَ” is an Arab exclamation, not an insult.)

الْكَلِمَاتُ Words · tap to see the meaning

مَهْمَا
whatever
امْرُؤٌ
a person / a man
خَلِيقَةٌ
a trait of character
تَخْفَى
is hidden
تُعْلَمْ
becomes known
سَئِمْتُ
I grew tired of
تَكَالِيفُ
burdens, duties
حَوْلٌ
a year

الْحِكْمَةُ The hikmah

You cannot hide your real character for long. Honesty, anger, pride, kindness: everything shows in time. So work on being truly good inside, not only looking good outside.

قَاعِدَةٌ Grammar spotlight

مَهْمَا means “whatever” and starts a condition. The verbs after it end with a sukūn (or a light kasra for the rhyme): تَكُنْ, تُعْلَمِ. Pattern: مَهْمَا + verb … + answer.

تَدْرِيبٌ Practice

مَاذَا تَعْنِي «مَهْمَا»؟
Answer: What does مَهْمَا mean?
الْجَوَابُ
Whatever.
هَلْ تَخْفَى الْأَخْلَاقُ عَلَى النَّاسِ دَائِمًا؟
Answer in Arabic: Do traits stay hidden from people forever?
الْجَوَابُ
لَا، تُعْلَمُ فِي النِّهَايَةِ.
كَمْ سَنَةً ذَكَرَ الشَّاعِرُ؟
Answer in Arabic: How many years did the poet mention?
الْجَوَابُ
ثَمَانِينَ حَوْلًا.

Mastery Checkpoint before moving to the next lesson

title: Mahfūdhāt 6: Imruʾ al-Qays — The Power of Words
interactive_html:
Your Goal: Recite two famous verses by Imruʾ al-Qays and notice how Arabic paints pictures with words.

نَبْذَةٌ About the poet

Imruʾ al-Qays ibn Ḥujr al-Kindī (died around 540 CE) lived before Islam. His Muʿallaqah is the best known poem of the pre-Islamic Arabs. We study these two lines for their language, rhythm and imagery, not for his way of life. Your teacher guides which lines we memorise.

الْأَبْيَاتُ Verses · tap to see the meaning

قِفَا نَبْكِ مِنْ ذِكْرَى حَبِيبٍ وَمَنْزِلِ … بِسِقْطِ اللِّوَى بَيْنَ الدَّخُولِ فَحَوْمَلِ
Stop, you two, and let us weep at the memory of a beloved and a dwelling at the sand-dune’s edge, between ad-Dakhūl and Ḥawmal.
مِكَرٍّ مِفَرٍّ مُقْبِلٍ مُدْبِرٍ مَعًا … كَجُلْمُودِ صَخْرٍ حَطَّهُ السَّيْلُ مِنْ عَلِ
(Describing his horse) charging, fleeing, advancing, retreating all at once, like a boulder hurled down by the torrent from above.

الْكَلِمَاتُ Words · tap to see the meaning

قِفَا
stop (you two)
نَبْكِ
let us weep
ذِكْرَى
memory
مَنْزِلٌ
dwelling
مُقْبِلٌ
advancing
مُدْبِرٌ
retreating
جُلْمُودٌ
boulder
السَّيْلُ
the flood / torrent

الْحِكْمَةُ The hikmah

A good speaker chooses words that make the listener see the picture. In one short line the poet shows a horse that is fast, strong and sure, using a rock rolling down a hill. Learn from this to describe things clearly when you speak and write.

قَاعِدَةٌ Grammar spotlight

Two people: قِفَا ends with alif, a command to two people (Arab poets often speak to two companions). Comparison: the letter كَ means “like”: كَجُلْمُودِ (like a boulder).

تَدْرِيبٌ Practice

كَيْفَ نَقُولُ: Like a boulder؟
Say in Arabic: like a boulder
الْجَوَابُ
كَجُلْمُودٍ.
مَاذَا تَعْنِي «قِفَا»؟
Answer: What does قِفَا mean and who is spoken to?
الْجَوَابُ
Stop! (to two people).
بِمَاذَا شَبَّهَ الشَّاعِرُ الْحِصَانَ؟
Answer in Arabic: What did the poet compare the horse to?
الْجَوَابُ
بِجُلْمُودِ صَخْرٍ حَطَّهُ السَّيْلُ.

Mastery Checkpoint before moving to the next lesson

title: Mahfūdhāt 7: Ḥassān ibn Thābit — Praising the Prophet ﷺ
interactive_html:
Your Goal: Recite two verses by Ḥassān ibn Thābit about the Prophet ﷺ and learn how to compare in Arabic.

نَبْذَةٌ About the poet

Ḥassān ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī (may Allah be pleased with him, died around 54 AH) was a Companion known as the poet of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He defended Islam and praised the Prophet ﷺ with his poetry.

الْأَبْيَاتُ Verses · tap to see the meaning

وَأَحْسَنُ مِنْكَ لَمْ تَرَ قَطُّ عَيْنِي … وَأَجْمَلُ مِنْكَ لَمْ تَلِدِ النِّسَاءُ
My eye has never seen anyone more handsome than you, and women have never given birth to anyone more beautiful.
خُلِقْتَ مُبَرَّأً مِنْ كُلِّ عَيْبٍ … كَأَنَّكَ قَدْ خُلِقْتَ كَمَا تَشَاءُ
You were created free of every flaw, as though you were created as you wished.

الْكَلِمَاتُ Words · tap to see the meaning

أَحْسَنُ
more handsome / better
أَجْمَلُ
more beautiful
قَطُّ
ever (with a negative: never)
تَلِدْ
she gives birth
النِّسَاءُ
women
خُلِقْتَ
you were created
مُبَرَّأٌ
free from
عَيْبٌ
flaw

الْحِكْمَةُ The hikmah

Ḥassān used his gift of speech for the truth and for the love of the Prophet ﷺ. Whatever gift Allah gave you, use it for good. Our greatest praise of the Prophet ﷺ is to love him, follow him and send salah upon him.

قَاعِدَةٌ Grammar spotlight

Comparing: the pattern أَفْعَلُ مِنْ means “more … than”: أَحْسَنُ مِنْكَ (more handsome than you), أَجْمَلُ مِنْكَ (more beautiful than you). Past negative: لَمْ + present verb means “did not”: لَمْ تَرَ.

تَدْرِيبٌ Practice

كَيْفَ نَقُولُ: more beautiful than you؟
Say in Arabic: more beautiful than you
الْجَوَابُ
أَجْمَلُ مِنْكَ.
مَاذَا تَعْنِي «لَمْ تَرَ»؟
Answer: What does لَمْ تَرَ mean?
الْجَوَابُ
You did not see.
بِمَاذَا لُقِّبَ حَسَّانُ؟
Answer in Arabic: What was Ḥassān known as?
الْجَوَابُ
شَاعِرُ رَسُولِ اللهِ ﷺ.

title: Mahfūdhāt 8: Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr — Repentance and the Light of the Prophet ﷺ
interactive_html:
Your Goal: Recite two verses from Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr’s poem for the Prophet ﷺ and learn how إِنَّ works.

نَبْذَةٌ About the poet

Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr was the son of Zuhayr (Lesson 5). At first he opposed Islam, then he came to the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah around 8 AH, repented and recited his poem Bānat Suʿād. It is reported that the Prophet ﷺ forgave him. The poem is known as the poem of the Burdah.

الْأَبْيَاتُ Verses · tap to see the meaning

بَانَتْ سُعَادُ فَقَلْبِي الْيَوْمَ مَتْبُولُ … مُتَيَّمٌ إِثْرَهَا لَمْ يُفْدَ مَكْبُولُ
Suʿād has gone far away, and my heart today is sick with love, enslaved after her, shackled and not ransomed.
إِنَّ الرَّسُولَ لَنُورٌ يُسْتَضَاءُ بِهِ … مُهَنَّدٌ مِنْ سُيُوفِ اللهِ مَسْلُولُ
The Messenger is truly a light by which people are guided, a sword of Indian steel drawn from among the swords of Allah.

الْكَلِمَاتُ Words · tap to see the meaning

بَانَتْ
she went far away
مَتْبُولٌ
sick with love
مُتَيَّمٌ
overcome by love
نُورٌ
light
يُسْتَضَاءُ بِهِ
is guided by it
مُهَنَّدٌ
Indian-steel sword
سَيْفٌ
sword
مَسْلُولٌ
drawn from its sheath

الْحِكْمَةُ The hikmah

A person can go back to the truth, however far he has gone. Kaʿb came with regret and was welcomed. The Prophet ﷺ is the light of guidance: whoever follows him is not lost. Never think it is too late to repent.

قَاعِدَةٌ Grammar spotlight

إِنَّ means “indeed” and the word after it ends with a fatḥa: إِنَّ الرَّسُولَ. The letter لَ in لَنُورٌ adds more emphasis: “truly a light”.

تَدْرِيبٌ Practice

كَيْفَ نَقُولُ: Indeed, the Messenger؟
Say in Arabic: Indeed, the Messenger
الْجَوَابُ
إِنَّ الرَّسُولَ.
بِمَاذَا وَصَفَ كَعْبٌ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ؟
Answer in Arabic: What did Kaʿb call the Prophet ﷺ?
الْجَوَابُ
نُورٌ يُسْتَضَاءُ بِهِ.
مَاذَا نَتَعَلَّمُ مِنْ تَوْبَةِ كَعْبٍ؟
Think: What do we learn from Kaʿb’s repentance?
الْجَوَابُ
Your own answer, then tell your teacher.

title: Mahfūdhāt 9: Al-Mutanabbī — Big Goals, Big Hearts
interactive_html:
Your Goal: Recite two famous verses by al-Mutanabbī and learn broken plurals through them.

نَبْذَةٌ About the poet

Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Mutanabbī (303–354 AH) is one of the greatest Arabic poets. His poetry is full of pride and wisdom; we memorise his wise lines, and your teacher chooses which ones.

الْأَبْيَاتُ Verses · tap to see the meaning

عَلَى قَدْرِ أَهْلِ الْعَزْمِ تَأْتِي الْعَزَائِمُ … وَتَأْتِي عَلَى قَدْرِ الْكِرَامِ الْمَكَارِمُ
Resolutions come in proportion to the people of resolve, and noble deeds come in proportion to the noble.
وَتَعْظُمُ فِي عَيْنِ الصَّغِيرِ صِغَارُهَا … وَتَصْغُرُ فِي عَيْنِ الْعَظِيمِ الْعَظَائِمُ
Small things look big in a small person’s eye, and great things look small in a great person’s eye.

الْكَلِمَاتُ Words · tap to see the meaning

قَدْرٌ
measure / proportion
الْعَزْمُ
firm resolve
الْكِرَامُ
the noble
الْمَكَارِمُ
noble deeds
تَعْظُمُ
becomes big
تَصْغُرُ
becomes small
الْعَظَائِمُ
great matters
صِغَارٌ
small things

الْحِكْمَةُ The hikmah

People act according to the size of their hearts. A person with high goals does great things and is not shaken by small problems. Set high goals for your studies, your memorisation and your character.

قَاعِدَةٌ Grammar spotlight

Broken plurals change the shape of the word: عَزِيمَةٌ ← عَزَائِمُ, مَكْرُمَةٌ ← مَكَارِمُ, عَظِيمَةٌ ← عَظَائِمُ. Learn them as whole words, like English “child → children”.

تَدْرِيبٌ Practice

مَا جَمْعُ «مَكْرُمَةٍ»؟
Answer in Arabic: What is the plural of مَكْرُمَةٌ?
الْجَوَابُ
مَكَارِمُ.
مَا ضِدُّ «تَعْظُمُ»؟
Answer in Arabic: What is the opposite of تَعْظُمُ?
الْجَوَابُ
تَصْغُرُ.
كَيْفَ تَأْتِي الْعَزَائِمُ؟
Answer in Arabic: How do resolutions come?
الْجَوَابُ
عَلَى قَدْرِ أَهْلِ الْعَزْمِ.
